definitions.explanation: A traditional form of Japanese poetry consisting of 17 morae (sound units) in a 5-7-5 pattern. Haiku typically focus on nature and seasonal imagery.

examples.japanese: {松尾芭蕉|まつおばしょう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{最|もっと}も→最も：01736_mottomo⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧⟦な→な：09497_na⟧{俳句|はいく}⟦{詩人|しじん}→詩人：03171_shijin⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Matsuo Basho is the most famous haiku poet in Japan.
The basic rule is to include a seasonal word in haiku.

examples.japanese: ⟦{学校|がっこう}→学校：00055_gakkou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{授業|じゅぎょう}→授業：00781_jugyou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{俳句|はいく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}った→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧。
examples.english: I wrote haiku in school class.

notes:
{俳句|はいく} is a traditional Japanese poetry form with strict structural requirements:
- 17 morae in 5-7-5 pattern
- Contains a ⟦{季語|きご}→季語：09561_kigo⟧ (seasonal reference word)
- Often includes a ⟦{切|き}れ{字|じ}→切れ字：09993_kireji⟧ (cutting word) for pause or emphasis

Famous haiku poets (⟦{俳人|はいじん}→俳人：09569_haijin⟧):
- {松尾芭蕉|まつおばしょう} (Matsuo Basho)
- {与謝蕪村|よさぶそん} (Yosa Buson)
- {小林一茶|こばやしいっさ} (Kobayashi Issa)

Related terms:
- ⟦{俳人|はいじん}→俳人：09569_haijin⟧ (haiku poet)
- ⟦{季語|きご}→季語：09561_kigo⟧ (seasonal word)
- ⟦{川柳|せんりゅう}→川柳：09660_senryuu⟧ (senryu - similar form but focuses on human nature rather than seasons)
